title_en: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning
title_zh: FewStepRL：用强化学习微调少步扩散模型
summary_en: This work systematically adapts reinforcement learning (RL) objectives to few-step diffusion models, which model an average velocity over an interval rather than the instantaneous velocity assumed by existing many-step RL objectives. The authors propose a three-phase approach—transformation, decomposition, and adaptation—that expresses objectives in x-space, decomposes gradients into a self-regression term toward a reference plus a reward augmentation, and computes anchors from few-step models along their transport or tangent. This yields few-step versions of FlowGRPO, AWM, DiffusionNFT, DiffusionOPSD, and ReFL in one modular codebase. Experiments show reward-gradient-based methods are most effective when the reward is differentiable.
summary_zh: 该工作系统性地将强化学习（RL）目标适配到少步扩散模型——这类模型建模的是区间上的平均速度，而现有多步 RL 目标针对的是瞬时速度。作者提出三阶段方法：变换、分解与适配，将各目标统一表达在 x 空间，把梯度分解为向参考的自回归项与奖励增强项，并从少步模型的传输末端或切线方向计算锚点。由此在一个模块化代码库中实现了 FlowGRPO、AWM、DiffusionNFT、DiffusionOPSD 和 ReFL 的少步版本。实验表明，当奖励可微时，基于奖励梯度的方法最为有效。
content_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a standard post-training method for diffusion models, but most RL objectives roll out the current policy at every iteration, and with a many-step sampler these rollouts typically dominate the cost of training. Few-step models cut this cost, yet they model an average velocity over an interval, whereas existing RL objectives are built for an instantaneous velocity with a many-step sampler. We adapt RL objectives to few-step models systematically in three phases, namely a transformation, a decomposition and an adaptation. The transformation to $x$-space expresses each objective we consider through a common policy prediction, at the clean end by default and at an explicitly marked level for transition or flow-map objectives, so that objectives stated over densities, velocities or rewards become comparable. The decomposition writes the gradient of each of these objectives as the sum of a self-regression toward a reference and a reward augmentation, so that a method reduces, at the gradient level, to a choice of anchors and weights. The adaptation computes each anchor from a few-step model at the end of its transport or along its tangent, with the instantaneous velocity recovered from the network itself or from an auxiliary network. This yields few-step versions of FlowGRPO, AWM, DiffusionNFT, DiffusionOPSD and ReFL in one modular codebase.
